description: We are RIDEX, a team participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We are passionate about space exploration, science, technology, and innovation. We are looking for motivated people interested in coding, software development, data analysis, graphic design, and problem-solving. Join us to share ideas, learn new skills, and build an innovative project together!
summary:
ECHO-RELIC // 2035 — Abandoned But Not Forgotten

We developed ECHO-RELIC // 2035, an interactive 3D space exploration and engineering platform that preserves and visualizes historical NASA missions and space artifacts.

The platform features an interactive 3D Moon globe, mission landing sites, spacecraft and rover locations, historical mission timelines, and verified NASA archival photographs. Users can explore lunar and deep-space missions, inspect coordinates, compare landing and final positions, and learn about significant engineering achievements.

Our project addresses the challenge of making historical space exploration data accessible, engaging, and meaningful. Instead of presenting scattered technical records, it combines verified NASA historical information with interactive 3D visualization and educational tools. It also supports offline exploration through a locally stored archive.

ECHO-RELIC // 2035 is important because it preserves humanity's space exploration heritage, makes complex engineering history easier to understand, and inspires future generations to explore science, technology, and space engineering.
details:
ECHO-RELIC // 2035

Abandoned But Not Forgotten — Interactive 3D Space Engineering Lab & Verified NASA Archive

1. What does your project do, and how does it work?

ECHO-RELIC // 2035 is an interactive space exploration platform that brings historical NASA missions and abandoned space artifacts back to life. Users can explore a 3D lunar globe, discover spacecraft and rover locations, examine mission timelines, view landing and final coordinates, and access authentic NASA archival photographs. The platform combines a verified local historical database with live NASA image APIs and an AI-powered assistant.

2. What benefits does it have?

It makes complex space exploration history accessible, educational, and engaging. Students, researchers, and space enthusiasts can explore real mission data through interactive visualizations instead of reading scattered technical documents.

3. What is the intended impact?

Our goal is to preserve humanity's space exploration heritage, increase public interest in planetary science, and inspire future generations of engineers, scientists, and explorers.

4. What tools did you use?

We used React, TypeScript, Vite, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, NASA APIs, NASA archival image services, Google Gemini AI API, and 3D visualization technologies. GitHub and Vercel were used for version control and deployment.

5. How is your project creative?

Our creativity comes from combining historical space artifacts, interactive 3D planetary exploration, verified scientific information, gamification, and AI assistance in one platform. Users do not simply read about missions; they explore them.

6. What factors did your team consider?

We focused on scientific accuracy, reliable NASA sources, accessibility, educational value, user experience, performance, and long-term preservation of historical space data. We also designed the platform to remain useful even when internet connectivity is limited.
